narrative.text: The cabinet room is not yet a cabinet room. Not really. It is a room where people who might become a cabinet are standing around a table that has seen seventeen previous governments — some that succeeded, some that didn't, one that ended with the Chancellor being carried out by security. You can feel the history in the furniture. Vyktor Reznik and Gregor Marić are already here. They are not having a conversation. They are having the kind of exchange that happens before a conversation, when positions are being staked out like territory.
We don't know what's in those files yet.
That's not a reassuring point, Vyktor.

Marić spots you in the doorway. His expression shifts — the argument is set aside, not resolved. He turns to face you with the particular energy of someone who has been losing a debate and believes the new arrival will see things his way.
